To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the purification of CSA from urine was possible, that the activity was not lost during the purification procedure, and that it could be measured in vitro.
we have developed a procedure for isolation of CSA from human urine and have produced specific antisera against it.

(1) CSA was purified from large batches of urine; (2) the purification was based on a new method of high flow dialysis; (3) the method was combined with adsorption to DE 52, treatment with Con A‐Sepahorse, Papain and Sephadex G‐100 gelfiltration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of CSA from large batches of urine and the production of specific antibodies against it.
the preparation of CSA from large batches of urine, its purification, its in vivo effects and the production of antisera to it.
the isolation of a protein with leucopoetic activity from human urine, the preparation of antisera to this protein and the characterization of its biological activity.

the method used for the isolation of CSA from human urine was suitable for the preparation of large quantities of highly enriched CSA.
the preparation of CSA from large batches of urine was successful.
the preparation of CSA from urine is feasible and reproducible.

the purification procedure described above, which was developed for large scale purification of CSA, has the potential to produce enough purified CSA for production of antisera in animals.
the method described is a useful tool for preparation of a large amount of highly enriched CSA from human urine.
